html:
Electronics Fundamentals
Why Three Phase Voltage Is 440V: The √3 Rule, 415 V Standard and Tolerance in Indian Supply

Indian electricians say 440 V, the standard says 415 V and IEC says 400 V, yet all three come from one √3 rule. Below we work through the phasor maths, the tolerance band behind the 440 V habit and a safe way to measure it.

√3 Rule Phasor Diagram IS 12360 Line Voltage Calculator Multimeter Test

Line voltage in a star connected supply is 1.732 times phase voltage, so a few volts of difference per phase moves the line figure between 400, 415 and 440 V. We cover the maths, the Indian standards and the field checks.

Hello everyone, today we are going to learn why three phase voltage is 440V in common Indian usage, how the √3 factor works and how to calculate and measure it.
Quick Answer

Why three phase voltage is 440V in India when the standard says 415 V?

Why three phase voltage is 440V comes from the √3 rule: line voltage equals 1.732 times phase voltage because the phases are 120° apart. India declares 240/415 V under IS 12360, and 415 V plus the old 6 percent supply tolerance gives about 440 V, which is the same as 254 V per phase. Example: 240 × 1.732 = 415.7 V and 254 × 1.732 = 439.9 V.

What Is the Real Reason Behind 440 V?

The answer to why three phase voltage is 440V is the √3 rule: line to line voltage is 1.732 times line to neutral voltage, so 254 V per phase gives 439.9 V. India actually declares 240/415 V, and 440 V is the upper end of that supply once tolerance is added.

Key Facts
  • Line voltage = √3 × phase voltage = 1.732 × Vph in a balanced star system.
  • 230 V gives 398.4 V, 240 V gives 415.7 V, 250 V gives 433.0 V and 254 V gives 439.9 V.
  • IS 12360 lists 240/415 V for India, not 230/400 V.
  • A 6 percent tolerance on 415 V gives 415 × 1.06 = 439.9 V.

If you are new to these terms, read our notes on single phase and three phase power first. The same ideas also explain the RMS values your meter shows.

How Is Line Voltage Calculated from Phase Voltage?

Line voltage is calculated by multiplying phase voltage by √3, which is 1.732. The factor appears because two phase voltages 120° apart are subtracted as phasors, not added as plain numbers.

VL = VR minus VY (phasor)
VL = 2 × Vph × cos 30°
VL = √3 × Vph = 1.732 × Vph

Picture R, Y and B as three equal arrows spaced 120° apart. The meter reading between R and Y is the line joining two arrow tips, and geometry gives it a length of 2 × Vph × cos 30°.

Since cos 30° is 0.866, twice that value is 1.732, the square root of 3. Our guide on phase angle in AC circuits covers the phasor maths in more depth.

Adding 254 + 254 gives 508 V, but the two phases never peak together, so the real difference is only 439.9 V.

Do You Know?

The Wikipedia article on three phase electric power states that line to line voltage is √3 times line to neutral voltage in a symmetrical star system. It lists red, yellow and blue as India's phase colours, hence R, Y and B.

Advertisement

Why Three Phase Voltage Is 440V When the Standard Says 415 V

The short reason why three phase voltage is 440V in everyday Indian speech is that 415 V plus its 6 percent tolerance lands at almost exactly 440 V. Transformer no load voltage and rounding did the rest.

IS 12360 from the Bureau of Indian Standards lists 240 V single phase and 415 V three phase as the preferred low voltages. Amendment 4 of November 2011 says the changeover from 240/415 V to the IEC style 230/400 V shall be kept in abeyance for the time being.

Phase voltageLine voltage (× 1.732)Where you meet it
230 V398.4 V (400 V)IEC 60038 world standard
240 V415.7 V (415 V)IS 12360 declared value for India
250 V433.0 VDistribution transformer no load rating
254 V439.9 V (440 V)Upper end of 415 V plus 6 percent

Rule 54 of the old Indian Electricity Rules 1956, since replaced by CEA safety regulations, limited low and medium voltage variation to 6 percent. So 415 × 1.06 = 439.9 V and 415 × 0.94 = 390.1 V, a healthy band of about 390 V to 440 V.

The same rules defined low voltage as not above 250 V and medium voltage as not above 650 V. That is why older Indian textbooks call the 415 V supply medium voltage.

Quick Tip

When a site engineer says the panel is 440 V, read it as a 415 V nominal system. Size equipment for 415 V and confirm it tolerates 440 V on light load nights.

A Government e Marketplace catalogue for 11 kV distribution transformers lists the no load ratio as 11000/433 to 250 V with a nominal LV system of 415 V. The secondary starts high to cover the voltage drop in cables under load.

Myth: India has an official 440 V three phase standard.
Fact: The declared Indian value is 240/415 V under IS 12360; 440 V is the rounded top of the tolerance band.
Myth: Three phase voltage is three times the phase voltage, so 3 × 230 = 690 V.
Fact: Phases are 120° apart, so line voltage is 1.732 × 230 = 398.4 V, not 690 V.
Myth: A reading of 440 V means the transformer is faulty.
Fact: A 440 V reading is still inside the 6 percent band of a 415 V supply.

Why Is 3 Phase 400V and Not 690V?

Three phase supply is 400 V and not 690 V because voltages that are 120° out of step cannot simply be added. Only the vector difference between two phases appears across a load connected line to line.

Electrical Technology shows that two 230 V phasors 120° apart give 2 × 230 × sin 60° = 398 V, rounded to 400 V. A 690 V result would need all three phases to peak together, which would make them one phase.

Star vs Delta: Where Line and Phase Voltage Differ

In a star connection line voltage is √3 times phase voltage, while in a delta connection line voltage equals phase voltage. So the 440 V question applies to star connected secondaries, and nearly every LV distribution transformer in India has one.

Star (Y) connection

Windings joined at a neutral point; 240 V line to neutral and 415 V line to line.

Best for: LV distribution with single phase loads
VL = 1.732 Vph
Delta (Δ) connection

Windings form a closed triangle with no neutral; each winding sees the full 415 V.

Best for: Motor windings, HV side of Dyn11 transformers
VL = Vph

Our comparison of star vs delta connection covers currents too, and the star delta transformation formula converts impedances.

Why star 240/415 V suits India
  • One transformer feeds both 3 phase motors at 415 V and single phase loads at 240 V.
  • Winding insulation only needs to handle phase voltage to earth.
Points to watch
  • A broken neutral can push 240 V loads toward 415 V and burn them.
  • Line readings near 440 V stress older 400 V rated equipment.
Advertisement

What Voltage Tolerance Is Allowed on a 415 V Supply?

A 415 V supply in India was allowed to move by 6 percent either way under Rule 54, which gives a band of about 390 V to 440 V. IEC 60038 uses 230/400 V with a band of plus or minus 10 percent at the supply terminals.

1.732Factor from phase to line
415 VDeclared Indian line value
6 %Old LV supply tolerance
439.9 V415 V plus 6 percent

The Schneider Electric Electrical Installation Guide lists India with both 400/230 V and 440/250 V entries and a frequency of 50 ± 1.5 Hz. So suppliers use the 440 V name as well, along with electricians.

IEC 60034 Zone A expects a motor to deliver rated output within plus or minus 5 percent of rated voltage. Check the motor nameplate details before connecting a 400 V motor to a panel that reads 440 V at night.

Unequal phase voltages hurt motors even more than a high average, as our article on voltage unbalance in motors shows with a numeric example.

Do You Know?

Under the Indian Electricity Rules 1956, high voltage supply was allowed 6 percent on the higher side but 9 percent on the lower side. Extra high voltage was allowed 10 percent higher and 12.5 percent lower.

PDF

Line Voltage Calculator and Solved Example

Enter a phase voltage to get line voltage, or set phase to 0 and enter a line voltage to get phase voltage. The tolerance field shows the healthy band.

Line and Phase Voltage Calculator (√3 Rule)
Result
Line 439.9 V, Phase 254.0 V, band 413.5 to 466.3 V at 6 percent
Solved example (calculator defaults)
Vph = 254 V, tolerance 6 %
VL = 1.732 × 254 = 439.9 V
Low limit = 439.9 × 0.94 = 413.5 V
High limit = 439.9 × 1.06 = 466.3 V
Reverse: 415 ÷ 1.732 = 239.6 V

This is the same maths as the free line and phase voltage calculator on our sister site. Once you know line voltage, use our guide on how to calculate three phase power to get kW from current and power factor.

A rise of only 24 V per phase, from 230 V to 254 V, lifts the line voltage by 41.5 V, from 398.4 V to 439.9 V.

How to Measure Line and Phase Voltage with a Multimeter

Measure line voltage between two phases and phase voltage between a phase and neutral, using a CAT III meter on AC volts. Healthy Indian readings are about 415 V and 240 V, with line close to 1.732 times phase.

Wear arc rated PPE chosen from our electrical PPE selection guide and work under an approved permit. A slipped probe on a busbar can start an arc flash.

1
Prepare
Select a CAT III 600 V or higher meter, set AC V and fit shrouded probes.
2
Prove
Test the meter on a known live source before and after the measurement.
3
Line to line
Measure RY, YB and BR, holding probes on the busbar test points.
4
Line to neutral
Measure RN, YN and BN and note all six readings.
5
Compare
Divide each line reading by 1.732 and compare with the phase readings.

If neutral to earth voltage is more than a few volts, check the earthing too, as our page on TN, TT and IT earthing systems explains.

Quick Tip

Log the six readings with time and load. A panel that reads 440 V at 2 AM and 400 V at noon points to tap settings and feeder loading.

Troubleshooting Wrong Three Phase Voltage Readings

Most wrong readings come from a loose neutral, a blown fuse, a wrong transformer tap or a meter on the wrong range. The table gives the likely cause for each symptom and what to check.

SymptomLikely causeCheck
Line 440 V or more at nightHigh tap, light load, capacitors onTap position, APFC relay steps
One phase 280 V, another 190 VLoose or broken neutralNeutral link torque, neutral current
One line reading near 240 VBlown fuse or open phaseFuse continuity, breaker contacts
All lines below 380 V at full loadUndersized cable, high dropVoltage at source and load end

A dip lasting seconds may be a sag rather than steady low voltage; see voltage sag, swell and flicker.

  • Line readings within about 390 V to 440 V on a 415 V system.
  • Phase readings within about 225 V to 255 V on a 240 V system.
  • No two line readings differ by more than about 2 percent.

For the theory behind the transformer side, the transformer working principle page explains turns ratio and regulation. Our own note on turns ratio and secondary voltage shows how 11000/433 V maps to 250 V per phase.

Why Three Phase Voltage Is 440V FAQ

What is the difference between line voltage and phase voltage with example?

Line voltage is measured between two lines, while phase voltage is measured between one line and neutral.

In a star supply with 240 V phase voltage, the line voltage is 1.732 × 240 = 415.7 V, which Indian panels label as 415 V.

Why three phase voltage is 440V in India if the standard is 415 V?

The declared value is 240/415 V under IS 12360, but 415 V plus 6 percent tolerance gives about 440 V.

Light loading at night and 433 V transformer secondaries often push readings near 440 V, so the 440 V name stuck on site.

How to calculate line voltage from phase voltage step by step?

Multiply the phase voltage by √3, which is 1.732, because two phasors 120° apart give 2 × Vph × cos 30°.

For example, 254 V phase voltage gives 1.732 × 254 = 439.9 V, and 230 V gives 398.4 V.

What is the common mistake when measuring 3 phase voltage with multimeter?

The most common mistake is using a low category meter or the wrong range on a live distribution board.

Always use a CAT III 600 V meter on AC volts, prove it on a known source and measure all six readings.

Which motor voltage rating should I choose for an Indian 415 V supply?

Choose a motor rated 415 V, because IEC 60034 Zone A expects rated output within 5 percent of rated voltage.

A 400 V motor on a supply that reaches 440 V runs 10 percent high, which raises magnetising current and heating.

What We Learn Today

  • Line voltage equals 1.732 times phase voltage in a star system because two phasors spaced 120° apart subtract as vectors rather than adding.
  • The familiar 440 V figure in India is simply 415 V plus the old 6 percent supply tolerance, which equals 439.9 V or 254 V per phase.
  • Measure line and phase voltage with a CAT III meter, record all six readings and check that line readings are 1.732 times phase readings.
